first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMB accounts and has inherited evidence of acquisition and revenue lift. Verify memory_73 because discount-driven gains may not translate into sustainable qualified revenue if retention or unit economics deteriorate. Verify memory_86 as the strongest alternative because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, while its evidence may stop at early adoption rather than long-term revenue. Current intent is a guarded, segment-targeted pricing test pending those records.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the onboarding flow. The verified source showed higher completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines with evidence aligned to sustainable growth. Reject promotional pricing because its verified cohort lost 12% retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Qualified-revenue impact from onboarding remains unmeasured, so the experiment should track retained qualified revenue alongside completion and activation.
